transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Hi. I’ve gotten so strict about what and how much I eat that I’m barely eating at all, and it’s starting to interfere with my work on job sites. I realized I needed to come in because it's really starting to affect my ability to do my job.
Are you restricting your eating because you’re afraid of gaining weight or feel your body is too fat, even if others say you’re thin? Or is there another main reason you’re barely eating?

I get completely panicked at the thought of gaining weight or looking "bigger" in my work overalls, especially if I think about eating something heavy like pizza. Honestly, though, I just see my current size as being in "job shape" so I can move easily on scaffolding, and I think everyone else is blowing my weight loss way out of proportion.

Have you lost so much weight that your periods have stopped or become irregular, or if that doesn’t apply, have others told you that you’re dangerously underweight even though you feel your size is normal? Also, do you ever make yourself vomit or use laxatives, diuretics, or excessive exercise after eating?

My parents and doctor are really worried and say I'm dangerously underweight because of my low blood pressure and fainting, but I think they're blowing it out of proportion since my size just helps me move easily on scaffolding. As for the other things, I don't vomit or use laxatives, and my periods haven't really been an issue.
What is your current height and weight, and what is the highest weight you would feel comfortable reaching? If your weight went above that, how would you feel or what would you do?

I don't actually know my exact weight right now, though I know my clothes are hanging off me and my tool belt needs extra holes punched. The thought of the scale going up at all fills me with absolute panic. I'm terrified that if I gain weight, I'll look bigger in my work overalls and my clients will notice.

When you look in the mirror or think about your body, do you still feel fat or too big in certain areas even though others say you’re very underweight? Or do you mainly feel your current low weight is normal and not a problem?

I don't see myself as fat; I just feel like I'm in "job shape" to move easily around scaffolding and tight stairwells. I truly believe my current weight is normal and that others are blowing things out of proportion when I'm really just tired from working so hard. But I do get terrified of gaining weight because I don't want to look "bigger" in my work overalls.
